howItWorks.lead: Offerra is a reverse real-estate market. The seller doesn't have to state a price — buyers submit their own offers and everyone can see how it's going.
howItWorks.step0Body: Whoever lists a property can give an indicative price — or leave the field empty and wait to see what people offer.
howItWorks.step1Body: The amount, nickname and date of every offer are visible to anyone. Who's behind the nickname stays unknown — until then.
howItWorks.step2Body: When the seller accepts an offer, the name, phone number and email are revealed to both sides at once. Or request a viewing — once the owner confirms it, it's the same thing.
howItWorks.step3Body: The "Messages" tab on a listing — always just the two of you, under your nickname. Phone numbers and emails can't be sent in messages; that's what an accepted offer or a viewing is for.
howItWorks.step4Body: Offerra is for individuals, not real-estate agencies. A listing, an offer and a user can all be reported, and a person reviews it.
howItWorks.section0Title: A reverse market — the price is optional
howItWorks.section0Para0: On a regular portal, the seller sets a price and the buyer either accepts it or walks away. Offerra works the other way round: you don't HAVE to give a price. You write what you're offering, and people tell you how much they're willing to pay.
howItWorks.section0Para1: If you do give an indicative price, it's only a guide — offers can be higher or lower. If you change it after publishing, the listing shows by how much. The price can't be edited silently.
howItWorks.section0Para2: For rentals every amount is MONTHLY; for sales it's the total.
howItWorks.section0Para3: A listing can only be published once it has a title, town, number of rooms, floor area and at least one photo — without that, nobody can decide if they're interested. Price, region and street are optional. A plot naturally doesn't need a room count.
howItWorks.section0Para4: You can pick the region before the town — then the town search is limited to it. Once you pick a town, the region is set from it; the town always decides.
howItWorks.section1Para0: The amount, nickname, date and status of every offer are visible to anyone — even signed out. That way you know whether you're in a bidding war or the only interested party.
howItWorks.section1Para1: Nobody finds out who's behind a nickname. Name and phone number are protected right in the database — they aren't released even technically, until there's a reason to.
howItWorks.section1Para2: The message you attach to an offer is NOT public. Only the seller and you can read it.
howItWorks.section1Para3: You have one live offer per listing. Raising it edits the same offer, it isn't a new one — otherwise the list could be flooded.
howItWorks.section1Para4: For rentals, a short questionnaire is attached to the offer (number of people, pets, rental length, employment). Only the listing owner sees it. Number of people is required.
howItWorks.section1Para5: You can also set your own validity period for each offer — for example 7 or 14 days — independently of the listing's own offer deadline. Once that validity expires, the offer is marked invalid in the list, the seller can no longer accept it, and it no longer counts toward the highest offer shown on the card. You'll get a notification when it expires.
howItWorks.section2Title: When your real identity is revealed
howItWorks.section2Para0: When the seller ACCEPTS an offer, the name, phone number and email are revealed to both sides at once. Before that, neither side has them.
howItWorks.section2Para1: Only the pair it concerns is revealed. No other interested party learns anything.
howItWorks.section2Para2: That's why it's worth filling in your name and phone number in Settings — without them the other side has no way to reach you after accepting an offer.
howItWorks.section3Title: Messages — you can ask right away
howItWorks.section3Para0: A listing's detail page has a "Messages" tab. You can write any time, even before you make an offer — that's exactly what it's for: asking what the listing doesn't tell you.
howItWorks.section3Para1: The same chat is also right on the INQUIRY DETAIL page — you don't need to be approached with a listing first. Handy when you want to check, before reaching out, whether what you're offering really fits what someone is looking for.
howItWorks.section3Para2: A conversation is ALWAYS just between two people. If a listing has ten interested parties, the seller has ten separate conversations, and interested parties don't know about each other. Nobody else can see someone else's conversation — not even technically. The same applies to inquiries.
howItWorks.section3Para3: Messages are sent UNDER YOUR NICKNAME. Messages by themselves don't reveal identity; name and phone number are revealed the same way as before — through an accepted offer or a viewing.
howItWorks.section3Para4: That's why phone numbers and emails CAN'T be sent in messages. The app rejects it and says why. Without that, the whole contact-reveal mechanism could be bypassed with a single message.
howItWorks.section3Para5: When someone messages you, you get a notification. The message content isn't in it — that stays private.
howItWorks.section4Para0: You don't have to wait for an offer to be accepted. The "Request a viewing" button sends a request — the owner sees it under your nickname, contact is NOT revealed yet.
howItWorks.section4Para1: The owner CONFIRMS or DECLINES the request in the Viewing tab. Only confirming reveals the name, phone number and email to both sides at once — the same mechanism as accepting an offer.
howItWorks.section4Para2: A cancelled or declined request isn't the end — the button reappears and you can request again. To stop this being abused for spam, requesting again is only possible after a short waiting period.
howItWorks.section4Para3: The app does NOT suggest or confirm a date. When and where you meet is something you agree by phone once contact is revealed.
howItWorks.section4Para4: What confirming does is written ABOVE the button, not only after. And it can't be undone — contact the other side has already seen isn't erased.
howItWorks.section4Para5: After the meeting, mark it as "I attended the viewing".
howItWorks.section5Title: Offer deadline — and what happens after it
howItWorks.section5Para0: A deadline is optional. Once you set one on a listing, a countdown runs on the card and in the detail ("Offers until… · X days left"), and after the date nobody can submit an offer any more — the database enforces this, not just a button in the app.
howItWorks.section5Para1: After the deadline, the listing is NOT deleted and doesn't disappear. You get a prompt on it: choose from the offers received, extend the deadline by 7 days, or archive the listing. Until you decide, it stays in the catalog with a "No longer accepting offers" label — so people can see nobody can offer on it any more.
howItWorks.section5Para2: An archived listing disappears from the catalog and nobody can offer on it any more. Offers already received stay in your overview.
howItWorks.section5Para3: The app does NOT send you a notification about a passed deadline — you'll see the prompt when you open the listing. We'd rather show it directly than have you wait for a notification that never comes.
howItWorks.section6Para0: Accepting an offer and closing the deal are TWO different things. Accepting means "let's agree", closing means "done" — paperwork usually happens in between, and it sometimes falls through.
howItWorks.section6Para1: Once an offer is accepted, the listing LOCKS: the price, floor area and terms can no longer be changed. What you agreed on has to stay exactly as it was at that moment. You can still add photos, but you can't delete existing ones — they're evidence of the property's condition.
howItWorks.section6Para2: When you close the deal, the listing disappears from the catalog and all other pending offers are closed. Their authors get a notification that the listing already has a buyer — without the winner's name or amount.
howItWorks.section6Para3: A deal can also be closed even if you agreed outside the app.
howItWorks.section7Para0: After a deal closes, both sides can rate each other with one to five stars and a few sentences.
howItWorks.section7Para1: A rating is FULLY PUBLIC — stars and text alike. It's visible next to the nickname and the listing.
howItWorks.section7Para2: That's deliberate: someone weighing a deal with a specific person needs context, not just a number. "4.6 stars" doesn't say whether the other side showed up on time.
howItWorks.section7Para3: Only the two people the deal concerned can rate each other, and only once. An unsuccessful bidder can't leave a rating — otherwise it could be used to retaliate for a rejection.
howItWorks.section7Para4: You can change your rating at any time.
howItWorks.section8Title: Inquiries — searching the other way round
howItWorks.section8Para0: In the Inquiries tab, you write what you're looking for. Owners can then reach out to you with their listing.
howItWorks.section8Para1: An inquiry speaks the SEEKER's language: "Buying" and "Looking to rent" instead of "For sale" and "For rent", which are used on listings. It's the same pair, just from the other side.
howItWorks.section8Para2: When someone reaches out to you, you get a notification and you'll find it in your inquiry's detail page. Tapping it opens the listing being offered to you — with photos, price and number of rooms, just like in the catalog. From there you can request a viewing exactly like on a listing you found yourself.
howItWorks.section8Para3: Being approached isn't a message. It's a record attached to your inquiry, and only someone with their own published listing can approach you. You can also message each other EARLIER — the inquiry's detail page has the same chat as a listing, under your nickname.
howItWorks.section8Para4: The budget is indicative, not a commitment. Your name and phone number don't appear on the inquiry — same as with offers.
howItWorks.section9Para0: A listing, an offer or a user can all be reported. Reasons include: fake listing (the property doesn't exist), scam (asks for a deposit, refuses a viewing), spam or advertising, inappropriate content, suspected agency, and Other.
howItWorks.section9Para1: NOTHING is deleted automatically. Every report is reviewed and decided by a person. An automatic system would also delete things it shouldn't.
howItWorks.section9Para2: If the rules were broken, an admin can hide the listing from the catalog or delete it. The owner can still see a hidden listing, along with the reason.
howItWorks.section9Para3: AND YOU'LL FIND OUT. When a report is confirmed, you get a notification with what happened and why — including the reason. You won't learn who reported you; otherwise reporting could become a reason for retaliation. The notification also states clearly that repeated violations can lead to the account being blocked.
howItWorks.section9Para4: A user can be blocked. A blocked account can't sign in or add anything; existing data stays and unblocking restores everything. It isn't a deletion.
howItWorks.section9Para5: Offerra is a market BETWEEN PEOPLE and is meant ONLY for individuals acting in their own name — an owner, co-owner, tenant or interested party. Real-estate agencies, brokers and agents are NOT allowed to use it, even through an account held by an individual. Everyone confirms this explicitly at registration, and the time of confirmation is kept on record.
howItWorks.section9Para6: A false confirmation breaks the terms and is grounds for immediate account blocking and deletion of listings. If you suspect an agency, there's a dedicated "Report an agency" button right next to the nickname.
howItWorks.section10Para0: One account can have at most five listings published at the same time.
howItWorks.section10Para1: It's a defense against flooding the catalog. Someone listing dozens of properties isn't the neighbor selling one flat — and Offerra is built exactly for that neighbor.
howItWorks.section10Para2: Draft listings don't count toward the limit, and archiving or closing a deal frees up a slot. If you hit the limit, the app tells you why and how many you have.
howItWorks.section11Para0: Save your current filters with a single tap and pull them up again later from the bar above the catalog.
howItWorks.section11Para1: Each saved search shows a number — how many listings match it and how many are new since you last opened it. Opening it resets the number to zero.
howItWorks.section11Para2: When a new listing matches a saved search, you get a notification.
howItWorks.section11Para3: A saved search is PRIVATE. Nobody but you can see what you're searching for. Delete it with a long press.
howItWorks.section11Para4: The search understands Slovak without diacritics and with inflected word forms — "Banskej" finds Banská Bystrica, "Košiciach" finds Košice.
howItWorks.section12Para0: Right at registration — after you set your nickname — Offerra asks whether you want notifications on your phone and shows you the full list of types right away. You set it up up front, instead of it suddenly starting to buzz one day while you go looking for where to turn it off.
howItWorks.section12Para1: For each type you choose whether you want it: a new offer on your listing, your offer being accepted or declined, a new inquiry matching your listing, a match with a saved search, interest in a viewing.
howItWorks.section12Para2: A disabled type sends nothing — neither in the app nor to your phone.
howItWorks.section12Para3: System and security notifications (for example, an account being blocked) can't be turned off. They always have to get through.
howItWorks.section12Para4: You'll find the same list any time in Settings and can change it. If you didn't grant permission at the start, the app won't nag you about it again — it will ask once more, after your first offer or first listing, once you already know what it's for.
howItWorks.section13Para0: Some people have a VERIFIED badge, next to a sentence saying exactly WHAT the admin verified — for example an ID document and a title deed.
howItWorks.section13Para1: The badge CANNOT be earned automatically or set by the user. It's granted exclusively by an admin, and the system won't accept it without a stated reason. A badge that can't say what it's based on would be just decoration.
howItWorks.section13Para2: The badge doesn't reveal anything else — name and phone number stay hidden just like for everyone else.
howItWorks.section14Para0: Listings can also be browsed on a map. The pin sits on the TOWN, though, not the building.
howItWorks.section14Para1: A seller can give a street, and the app suggests it from the Slovak Ministry of Interior's address register, but without a house number. The exact address gets worked out in person.
howItWorks.section14Para2: The app doesn't access your location. The position shown on the map is the town's location from a public reference list.

propertyTabs.offerAcceptedNote: The offer is accepted. You'll find the seller's contact in the "Viewing" tab.

propertyTabs.withdrawConfirmBody: It will disappear from the list as active.
propertyTabs.offersClosedNote: This listing no longer accepts offers — new offers can't be submitted.
propertyTabs.priceIndicativeNote: The price is only indicative. You can offer more or less — the seller decides.
propertyTabs.wantToOffer: I want to make an offer
propertyTabs.mustSignInNote: Offers are public, but only a signed-in person can submit one — otherwise there'd be nobody to reveal contact to if the seller accepts it.
propertyTabs.publicOffersNote: Amounts and nicknames are public. Who's behind them is only revealed to the one whose offer the seller accepts. The message attached to an offer isn't public — only the seller and the person who wrote it can read it.
propertyTabs.viewingSignInNote: Only a signed-in person can request a viewing. The owner confirms the request, and only then do you both reveal name, phone number and email to each other — otherwise there'd be no way to arrange a date.
propertyTabs.ratingsOwnerNote: This is your reputation across all deals, not just this listing — it's exactly what bidders see too.
propertyTabs.ratingsBidderNote: These are {{nickname}}'s ratings from ALL of their deals, not just this listing. A listing sells once; a reputation is built over longer.
propertyTabs.ratingsNotYetNote: Rating is only possible after a deal closes, and only by the two people who closed it together.
propertyTabs.offerExpiredNote: Your offer's validity has expired. If you're still interested, submit a new one.

inzeratEdit.cannotPublishTitle: This listing can't be published yet
inzeratEdit.publishedToast: Published — the listing is in the catalog
inzeratEdit.deleteBody: All photos will be deleted too. You'll have a few seconds to undo.
inzeratEdit.lockedBody:
You've accepted an offer, so the title, price, area, and terms can no longer change. What you agreed on must stay as it was at that moment.

You can still add more photos — they don't change the substance of the agreement. But existing ones can't be deleted or replaced; they're evidence of the state of things.

If you really need a change, contact {{email}}.
inzeratEdit.formLead: While the listing is a draft, no one but you can see it. The price is optional — leave it blank if you want people to propose their own.
inzeratEdit.visibleOnlyToYou: Only you can see it until you publish
inzeratEdit.photosHint: At least one is required. Added one at a time — the first becomes the cover.

inzeratEdit.priceHint: Leave blank if you'd rather hear offers without naming a figure. Buyers submit their own offers anyway — this is just a guide.
inzeratEdit.monthlyCostsHint: Reserve fund, common areas, management. Not rent or a deposit — payable after purchase too.
inzeratEdit.rentSectionHint: All optional — but the more you fill in, the fewer questions you'll get.

admin.needsAttentionHint: Three different people reported the same thing — or someone reported fraud.
admin.repeatOffendersHint: Three or more CONFIRMED reports against the same person — across all their listings and offers. The app never blocks anyone automatically; blocking is done in the Users section.
admin.reportsHint: "Mark as resolved" means you took action — the reported user is notified, and for a listing you decide right there whether to hide it. "Dismiss" means the report was unfounded; nothing is sent to the reported user then. Neither one DELETES anything — the owner still sees a hidden listing along with the reason.
admin.hidePropertyHintDefault: Defaults to yes for this reason. Uncheck if the listing should stay published.
admin.hidePropertyHintManual: Decide for yourself for this reason — it can also be fixed by editing the text.
admin.resolvedHiddenToast: Resolved, the listing is hidden. The user has {{total}} confirmed reports.
admin.resolvedToast: Resolved. The user has {{total}} confirmed reports.
admin.repeatViolationsBody: This account has {{total}} confirmed reports. You can block it in the Users section — the app won't do it on its own.
admin.hidePropertyBody: It disappears from the catalog but stays in the database and with the owner.
admin.propertyHiddenToast: The listing is hidden from the catalog.
admin.deletePermanentlyBody: Photos and offers are deleted too. This can't be undone.
admin.verifyUserBody: Write WHAT you verified — this sentence appears to people next to their badge.
admin.verifyPlaceholder: Proof of identity and title deed
admin.grantAdminBody: Really make {{nickname}} an admin? They'll get full access to this console — able to see reports, hide listings, and block accounts.
admin.revokeAdminBody: {{nickname}} will lose access to the console. Their account and data remain untouched.
admin.blockUserBody: They won't be able to sign in or add anything. Their existing data stays. You'll have a few seconds to undo.
admin.unblockUserBody: They'll be able to sign in and add things again.
admin.noOwnScreenNote: Doesn't have its own screen yet — act on it via the Users list.
admin.propertiesHint: "Hide from catalog" doesn't delete the listing — the owner still sees it along with the reason and it can be restored. "Delete permanently" also deletes photos and offers and can't be undone.
admin.usersHint:
A blocked user can't sign in or add anything, and their account doesn't receive notifications. Their existing listings and offers remain, and unblocking restores everything — it's not a deletion.

Only another admin can make someone an admin. You can't change your own role, and the app won't let the last admin be removed — that would leave it with none. Every role change is logged.
admin.limitUpdatedToast: The limit is now {{value}}. Takes effect immediately, no new build needed.
admin.currentlyLimit: Currently: {{value}}. The change applies immediately on the next publish attempt.
admin.topListersHint: A prompt to take a look, not an accusation. "No declaration" means an account from before the confirmation was introduced, not an admission.
admin.noListingsYet: No one has a listing yet.
admin.susThresholdsHint: From how many listings/percent the account below appears. Takes effect immediately, no new build needed.
admin.rateLimitHint: The server rejects an action once the same account exceeds it within the given window. Takes effect immediately, no new build needed.
admin.floodHint: Offers on an unusually large number of DIFFERENT listings in a short time — a prompt to look, not an accusation.
admin.lowballHint: Significantly below the guide price across MULTIPLE listings — once is negotiation, repeated is a pattern.
admin.shillSection: REPEATEDLY OFFERS TO THE SAME OWNER ({{count}})
admin.shillHint: One buyer repeatedly makes offers on the same seller's listings — with open offers, this could be artificially inflating the price via a second account.
admin.shillTargetNote: Offers to owner {{owner}} on {{count}} different listings

report.reasonFakeListing: Fake listing — the property doesn't exist
report.reasonAgency: Agency/broker — posing as a private individual
report.reasonFraud: Fraud — asks for a deposit, refuses a viewing
report.alreadyReportedBody: You've already reported this, once is enough.
report.acceptedToast: Report received, we'll take a look
report.nothingDeletedLead: Nothing is deleted automatically. A person reviews the report and decides.
report.noteHint: The more specific, the faster it can be reviewed.
report.notePlaceholder: e.g. the same photo appears on another listing with a different address

catalog.title: Properties
catalog.emptyBody: No published listings. You can add the first one — and you don't have to name a price.
catalog.noMatchBody: Try removing a filter or making your search broader.

login.subtitle: Properties for sale and rent
login.why: Sign in with Apple or Google — a verified account means a real person stands behind every listing.
login.legalPrefix: By signing in you agree to the

nickname.nicknameTooShort: The nickname must be at least 3 characters.
nickname.ageRequired: You can't register without confirming your age — only adults can list properties or make offers.
nickname.phoneRequired: Enter a phone number. Without it, the other party has no way to reach you for a viewing or after accepting an offer.
nickname.ownNameRequired: You can't register without confirming you're acting in your own name. Offerra is a market between people, not for real-estate agencies.
nickname.title: What should we call you?
nickname.lead: Your offers will be visible under your nickname to everyone — even signed-out visitors. Your real name and phone number stay hidden and only appear once someone accepts your offer or requests a viewing.
nickname.hiddenSection: HIDDEN DETAILS — REVEALED ONLY ON AGREEMENT
nickname.hiddenNote: No one sees these — they're revealed exclusively to the other party, and only once they request a viewing or an offer is accepted.
nickname.fullNameHintSuggested: We filled it in from your sign-in. Feel free to change it.
nickname.fullNameHintManual: You can also add it later in Settings.
nickname.phoneHint: Without it, the other party has no way to arrange a viewing with you or reach you after accepting an offer. It stays hidden until it's needed.
nickname.adultLabel: I am 18 years old or older.
nickname.adultHint: Only adults can list properties or make offers.
nickname.ownNameLabel: I am acting in my own name as an individual — I am not a real-estate agency or broker.
nickname.ownNameHint: Offerra is a market between people. A false confirmation is grounds for blocking the account.

upozornenia.systemDeniedBody: You can only turn it on in your phone's settings now: Settings → Offerra → Notifications. Set the choices below anyway — they apply to in-app notifications and will take effect as soon as you enable permission later.
upozornenia.title: Want to know about it?
upozornenia.lead: Offerra can let you know on your phone when something happens with your listing or an offer you made — even with the app closed.
upozornenia.bulletOffer: Someone made an offer on your listing.
upozornenia.bulletAccepted: Your offer was accepted — that's when contact details are revealed.
upozornenia.unavailable: This app version doesn't support push notifications yet. You'll have notifications in the app's bell.
upozornenia.granted: Notifications are on. You can turn them off anytime in Settings.
upozornenia.denied: Your phone blocked notifications. You can enable them in your phone's settings: Settings → Offerra → Notifications.
upozornenia.whatToSendHint: Everything is on and arrives immediately. Anything you turn off here won't reach your phone or the app's bell. You can change this anytime in Settings.
upozornenia.skipNote: Without permission the app works normally — you'll find notifications by the bell.

legal.openWebVersion: Open the public version in your browser

novinky.lead: A list of changes, newest first. If you don't see something from the latest entry in the app yet, the update hasn't reached you — compare the row below with what you have on the Mine tab.

savedSearches.duplicateNameError: You already have a saved search with this name.
savedSearches.lead: A saved search remembers the filter and sort order. The number shows how many listings were added since you last opened it. Only you see it.

contactCard.hint: Seen ONLY by the other party of an accepted offer, and only once it's accepted. No one else can access them — not even technically.
contactCard.emailChangeHint: The email is changed via sign-in, not here.
contactCard.missingWarning: Without a name and phone number, the other party has no way to reach you after accepting an offer.

mortgage.useTopOffer: The top offer is {{amount}} — use it
mortgage.rateHint: The default number is an estimate, not a bank offer. Your bank will tell you the actual rate; edit it here.
mortgage.emptyState: Enter a price and the app will calculate an estimated payment. The seller didn't have to give a price — it's optional in Offerra.
mortgage.disclaimer: An approximate estimate, not a bank offer. Doesn't account for fees, insurance, or property tax, and says nothing about whether a bank will approve the loan. Offerra isn't a financial advisor — only a bank can give you the real figure.

messages.contactBlocked: The message looks like it contains a {{reason}}. Sharing contact details in messages isn't allowed — contact is revealed automatically once an offer is accepted or a viewing is arranged.
messages.loginRequired: You need to sign in to send messages. The conversation is always just between you and the other party — no one else sees it.
messages.silentOfferNote: Made an offer, you haven't messaged yet. Reach out first.
messages.noOneWroteYet: No one has written to you yet. You have a separate conversation with each buyer — they don't know about each other.
messages.conversationHint: Only you two see this conversation. Names and phone numbers aren't revealed in it — that happens once an offer is accepted or a viewing is arranged.
messages.nothingYet: Nothing yet. Send the first message — for example, what you'd like to ask before making an offer.
messages.inputPlaceholder: e.g. Is the kitchen included in the price?

demandMessages.silentOutreachNote: Reached out to you with their listing, you haven't messaged yet. Reach out first.

ratingCard.starsRequired: Pick a number of stars — the rating won't save without it.
ratingCard.title: Rating
ratingCard.howWasIt: How did it go with {{nickname}}? The rating is PUBLIC — the stars and text are visible to anyone considering a deal with them. Write it so it helps the next person.
ratingCard.commentHint: Everyone sees it next to their nickname. Keep it factual — it's about the deal, not the person.
ratingCard.commentPlaceholder: e.g. smooth deal, arrived on time

streetPicker.hintWithCity: No house number — you'll agree on the exact address once an offer is accepted. Streets come from the Address Register; you can also type a different one.
streetPicker.hintWithoutCity: Pick a town first, then we'll suggest streets from the Address Register.
streetPicker.label: Street (optional)

cityPicker.hintWithRegion: Searching in the {{region}} region. The map position fills in based on the town; we don't ask for an exact address.
cityPicker.hintWithoutRegion: The region and map position fill in based on the town. We don't ask for an exact address.
cityPicker.searchPlaceholderWithRegion: e.g. Springfield — searching in the {{region}} region
cityPicker.emptyWithRegion: Nothing found in the {{region}} region. Try a different part of the name, or change the region above.
cityPicker.emptyGeneric: Nothing found. Try a different part of the name.

photo.tooLarge: The photo is {{mb}} MB, the limit is 8 MB. Try a smaller one.

pushPrompt.bodyListing: When someone makes an offer on your listing or requests a viewing, we'll let you know — even with the app closed.
